headline: Reframed under the corrected account model: this is a one-account operation running roughly 500 actions a day through the main profile, and that overload is the leading suspect for both the action blocks and the 1.3% reply rate. The account fleet buildout is now the strategic move; booking the 6 live unbooked replies is the free cash this week.

sections.title: The bottleneck
sections.text: Single-account concentration. Doctrine correction from Ryan: there is no three-account fleet yet, one main account carries ~100 initials a day plus the follow up load (~440 to 540 logged actions daily), with Instagram action blocks as the ceiling and an unwarmed alt that replies worse. That overload plausibly explains the blocks (MEASURED: volume dips and the Aug 3 note), the reply rate of 1.3% on 713 sends (MEASURED, gate met, floor 3%), or both. Per the message-dead rules, copy cannot be blamed until account throttling is ruled out.

sections.title: Levers, ranked by cash
sections.text: 1. Reply rate 1.3% to 3%: roughly EUR 2,000 a month at current pace (MEASURED input, baseline show and close), and the fix order is account health first, copy second. 2. Booking rate 11.1% to 25%: roughly EUR 2,000 a month, now nearly equal to the reply lever; 9 replies sits one short of the 10-reply gate, and the concrete version costs nothing: Owen (11d), mrplusmoney (10d) and cblez (10d) are stale past a week, Adam and Matt are aging at 3 days, Ryan, rahul and Caleb replied within 24 hours and are live right now. Speed to lead is doctrine. 3. Account fleet to three warmed profiles: not directly priceable yet (HYPOTHESIS), but it is the only lever that raises the volume ceiling, removes block risk from the main brand asset, and tests the profile-credibility hypothesis at once. 4. Cash per close 5k to 7.5k: small today, scales with every upstream fix.

sections.title: Strategic moves
sections.text: One constraint at a time. This week: get a delivery date from the warm-up vendor for accounts 2 and 3 and judge them on looking credible, not just aged, per the account quality hypothesis. Do not push the main account harder into blocks; the ceiling is the ceiling until the fleet lands. Before the next booked call, load the pre-call sequence with testimonials and results assets, the Kyle Cooke rule. And hold the frame on August: with EUR 5k upfront on payment plans, calls booked now are mostly September cash, so this month is scored on booked calls.

sections.title: What you would miss
sections.text: One more reply hits the 10-reply gate, and at 1 of 10 the booking verdict goes officially red; working the 6 unbooked replies before that gate trips is the difference between a fixed number and a formal failure. The lead scheduler sheet still shows nothing updated since 31 July while the EOD form logs 400 follow ups a day; two records of the same work still disagree. Replies are clustering: 5 of 9 landed in the last 72 hours (sample too small for a verdict, worth watching). Commission liability accrues at 7.5% from the first collected euro.

sections.title: Do not touch
sections.text: The daily block schedule, the ladder design, comment logging (now flowing daily at ~97% of initials, fix confirmed working), EOD discipline (12 for 12 days), and evening reply timing. All working. Tenet 10.

sections.title: Training questions for Ryan
sections.text: 1. What exactly does the EOD follow up number count: DMs only, or comments, likes and story views too? The answer determines how far past block-safe limits the main account is actually running. 2. When do accounts 2 and 3 arrive from the warm-up vendor, and will Rhys tag which account each reply lands in once they are live?
